title: Impaired Flow and Physiology in Coronaries With Anomalous Origin From the Opposite Sinus of Valsalva.
authors: Mauro Lo Rito; Mattia Squillace; Mauro Luca Agnifili; Antonio Rosato; Serena Anglese; Adele Chiavetta; Camilla Muritti; Miriam Deamici; Jessica Negri; Andrea Attanasio; Gianluigi Guida; Giandomenico Disabato; Francesco Secchi; Michele Conti; Alessandro Frigiola; Massimo Chessa; Alessandro Giamberti; Francesco Bedogni
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA) high-risk anatomical features (intramural segment, acute take-off angle, slit-like ostium) cause coronary stenosis leading to myocardial infarction. How these features alter coronary physiology remains unclear.
We aimed to evaluate their impact on coronary blood supply using continuous thermodilution.
We prospectively enrolled 51 AAOCA patients undergoing continuous thermodilution. Subjects were classified into an ischemic risk (IR) group (intramural segment, acute angle, oval or slit ostium) or non-ischemic risk (no-IR) group. Non-anomalous coronary arteries served as controls. We measured absolute coronary blood flow (CBF) and microvascular resistance.
Subjects (median age 48.4 years) presented mostly with angina, syncope, and arrhythmia. Final analysis included 48 AAOCA cases (31 IR, 17 no-IR) and 45 controls. The IR group had a median IM length of 9 mm, take-off angle of 31.9°, and a slit-like or oval ostium. The no-IR group had a median angle of 51.5° and an oval or round ostium. At rest, absolute CBF and microvascular resistance showed no significant differences among groups. However, during hyperemia, the IR group had significantly reduced CBF compared to controls (179 vs. 290 mL/min, p = 0.015). The IR group demonstrated higher microvascular resistance at rest (1473 vs. 1150, p = 0.024) and during hyperemia (433 vs. 305, p = 0.012), indicating persistently increased coronary vascular tone.
High-risk anatomical features of AAOCA are associated with altered coronary physiology. An intramural segment, acute take-off angle, and slit-like or oval ostium are linked to reduced hyperemic coronary blood flow due to increased microvascular resistance.

title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Yuki Hida; Teruhiko Imamura; Hiroshi Ueno; Koichiro Kinugawa; Masanori Yamamoto; Takahiro Tokuda; Tetsuro Shimura; Shinichi Shirai; Kenichi Ishizu; Yohei Ohno; Fumiaki Yashima; Toru Naganuma; Yusuke Watanabe; Futoshi Yamanaka; Gaku Nakazawa; Masahiko Noguchi; Masaki Izumo; Masahiko Asami; Hidetaka Nishina; Hiroto Suzuyama; Kazumasa Yamasaki; Kenji Nishioka; Daisuke Hachinohe; Yasushi Fuku; Toshiaki Otsuka; Kentaro Hayashida; OCEAN‐TAVI Investigators
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.
We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.
We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.
The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.
A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.

title: Short-Term Complications of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PROLONG-TAVR).
authors: Mauricio Castillo-Perez; Humberto De León-Gutiérrez; Carlos Jerjes-Sánchez; Lillian Royzman-Rivera; Jose Gildardo Paredes-Vazquez; Vicente Jimenez-Franco; Paola Gutiérrez-Gallegos; Maria J Cabada-Garcia; Jahir Rodriguez-Rivera; Enrique Paredes-Gutierrez; Renata Quevedo-Salazar; Juan F Sanchez-Avila
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: To estimate the cumulative incidence of short-term complications across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) prostheses used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol. Observational studies published from 2002 through May 2024 that included patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing predominantly transfemoral TAVR and reported prosthesis-specific complications were eligible. Although the original protocol intended to evaluate both short- and long-term complications, long-term outcomes were too sparse and inconsistently reported for robust pooled analyses; therefore, the present analysis focuses on short-term complications. Pooled cumulative incidences were calculated using random-effects models. We included 242 studies comprising 181,187 patients. SAPIEN 3 had the lowest incidence of moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) (1.04%, 95% CI 0.69-1.55) and stroke (1.87%, 95% CI 1.64-2.14), whereas ACURATE neo2 had the lowest incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) (7.7%, 95% CI 5.82-10.11). Evolut PRO and SAPIEN 3 showed among the lowest rates of major vascular complications (3.56%, 95% CI 2.77-4.57 and 3.87%, 95% CI 3.22-4.66, respectively) and major or life-threatening bleeding (2.96%, 95% CI 2.09-4.17 and 4.8%, 95% CI 4.04-5.69, respectively). Short-term complications have decreased with newer-generation THV prostheses. PVL remains more frequent with self-expanding valves, whereas PPI is the most frequent complication and is generally less frequent with balloon-expandable valves and ACURATE neo2. Stroke rates have changed little across newer generations, and annular rupture, coronary artery obstruction, and valve embolization remain rare (< 1%).

title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
authors: Adem Şafak; Emre Karakaya; İlgin Demir; Esra Baskın; Sedat Yıldırım; Atilla Sezgin; Mehmet Haberal
abstract: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
authors: Amber van Broekhoven; Eveline P M van Doorn; Wieteke Broeders; Aysun Cetinyurek-Yavuz; Erwin S Zegers; Mihai G Netea; Alexander B A Vonk; Niels van Royen; Hans W M Niessen; Jan H Cornel; Niels P Riksen; Saloua El Messaoudi
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

title: RNA-Based Therapies for Lipoprotein(a) Reduction: Antisense Oligonucleotides, Small Interfering RNAs, and Emerging Platforms.
authors: Vibhu Parcha; Vera A Bittner
abstract:
Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent, genetically determined, and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Elevated Lp(a) affects approximately 20% of the global population and is not meaningfully modified by lifestyle intervention or existing lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy. This review summarizes the biology of Lp(a) as a therapeutic target, evaluates the efficacy of currently available lipid-lowering agents against this target, and describes the mechanistic principles, clinical evidence, and unresolved questions associated with RNA-based and emerging small-molecule and gene-editing approaches to Lp(a) reduction.
Four RNA-directed agents targeting hepatic apolipoprotein(a) [apo(a)] synthesis have entered phase 2/3 development. This includes pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), and olpasiran, zerlasiran, and lepodisiran, which are N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated small interfering RNAs (siRNAs). Phase 2 data demonstrate Lp(a) reductions ranging from 79% to approximately 97% on a placebo-adjusted basis, approaching the practical limit of apo(a) suppression, with favorable short-term safety profiles. A fifth, structurally distinct siRNA conjugated with GalNAc at both strand termini has recently completed first-in-human testing, sustaining reductions up to 97% through 48 weeks after a single dose without injection-site reactions. Recently, the topline results of phase 3 Lp(a) HORIZON (pelacarsen) were released and demonstrate a substantial Lp(a) reduction without meeting the trial's primary composite cardiovascular endpoint. Two further outcomes trials, OCEAN(a)-Outcomes (olpasiran) and ACCLAIM-Lp(a) (lepodisiran), remain ongoing. An oral small molecule, muvalaplin, achieved comparable reductions in phase 2 testing. Lastly, early non-human primate data, together with a completed phase 1 trial of an analogous CRISPR-Cas9 construct targeting a related hepatic lipid gene, support the feasibility of a CRISPR-Cas9-based gene-editing approach capable of durable apo(a) suppression from a single administration. The pharmacology of Lp(a) suppression is now well characterized across three distinct therapeutic modalities. Whether the magnitude of biochemical reduction observed translates into a meaningful and safe reduction in cardiovascular events across different populations remains undetermined and will be addressed by the ongoing outcomes trials.

title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.
authors: Emiliano Fiori; Dimitri Buytaert; Michele Mattia Viscusi; Raffaella Mistrulli; Sara Corradetti; Tatyana Storozhenko; Anthony Kechichian; Nikolaos Stalikas; Eric Wyffels; Riet Dierckx; Emanuele Barbato; Ward A Heggermont; Jeroen Dauw; Jozef Bartunek; Marc Vanderheyden
journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmax and preload-adjusted indices [dP/dtmax/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmin, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/dtmax (Δ + 150 mmHg/s; P = 0.004), without improvement in dP/dtmin (P = 0.329) or τ (P = 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/dtmax (P < 0.001), dP/dtmax/LVEDP (P = 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (P = 0.031), while improving dP/dtmin (Δ + 56 mmHg/s; P = 0.050) and τ (P = 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (P = 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (P = 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis. Controlled atrial pacing revealed blunted force-frequency and relaxation-frequency responses before valve replacement, despite preserved ejection fraction, with rapid recovery after afterload relief. These findings show that impaired myocardial reserve in pressure-overload remodeling is functionally reversible and tightly linked to loading conditions.

title: Pathogenesis, screening, and diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Kendra M Gilreath; Darrell B Newman; Steve R Ommen; Jeffrey B Geske
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a common heritable heart disease. The disease is genetically, anatomically, and clinically heterogeneous. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern but has allelic heterogeneity, incomplete penetrance, and variable expressivity. Beyond family screening, clinical evaluation for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is often prompted by identification of symptoms or detection of a heart murmur, additionally, abnormal electrocardiogram or imaging results performed for another reason can provide evidence. Evaluation should include obtaining a patient's history, a physical examination, cardiac imaging, and, often, genetic testing. Prognosis is variable; major causes of morbidity and mortality are caused by sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation with associated stroke risk. An understanding of the pathogenesis at the genetic, cellular, and individual levels helps clinicians to implement appropriate screening, recognise clinical manifestations, and improve the treatment of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The understanding of this condition is evolving, with recent advances and insights into its pathogenesis, refinement of risk stratification, and use of artificial intelligence in screening, diagnosis, and prognostication.

title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
authors: Panagiotis Theofilis; Panayotis K Vlachakis; George Koutsopoulos; Ioannis Kachrimanidis; Panagiotis Iliakis; Nikolaos Ktenopoulos; Polykarpos Christos Patsalis; Konstantinos Toutouzas; Konstantinos Tsioufis
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.
This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.
Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
authors: Bo Li; Linlin Dai; Yujie Liu; Zijuan Han; Yun Tang; Xingrui Chen; Aoxiang Zhang; Xuan Ma; Pengyu Zhou; Xi Jia; Wenqing Xu; Kaisaierjiang Aisikaier; Shengyao Han; Fen Sa; Kai Yang; Kankan Zhao; Chaowu Yan; Shihua Zhao; Xiuyu Chen
abstract:
The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR.
Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE.
In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement using transcatheter aortic valve implants in the mitral position: a UK multicentre experience.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
authors: Taeil Yang; Joonpyo Lee; Kil Yoon Pack; Kyung Eun Ha; Youngwoo Jang; Woong Chol Kang; Jeonggeun Moon
abstract:
Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear.
This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint.
Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group.
In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

title: Fibro-Inflammatory Signaling, Fibrosis, and Microvascular Ischemia as Convergent Translational Substrates of Sudden Cardiac Death in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
authors: Antonio da Silva Menezes Junior; Isabela Jube Wastowski; Lilian Carla Carneiro
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains an important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD), but the biological determinants of ventricular arrhythmic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. This systematic translational review examined whether fibro-inflammatory signaling, fibrotic remodeling, and microvascular ischemia represent convergent components of the arrhythmogenic substrate in HCM. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Of 167 records, 37 full-text reports were assessed and 11 studies included. Fibrosis emerged as the most clinically mature substrate marker, while microvascular ischemia appeared to amplify electrical instability, particularly in remodeled myocardium. Molecular and tissue studies suggested upstream fibro-inflammatory programs involving activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix dysregulation, SMAD/TGF-beta signaling, CRLF1/LIFR-JAK-STAT signaling, and altered multicellular communication. Overall, the evidence supports an integrated mechanism-to-substrate model, but prospective outcome-validated studies are needed before these biological layers can refine SCD risk stratification beyond established clinical and imaging markers in contemporary HCM practice.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
authors: Felipe Diez-Delhoyo; Jorge Sanz-Sanchez; Guillem Muntane-Carol; Ignacio Jesus Amat-Santos; Juan Francisco Oteo Dominguez; Ricardo Rivera-Lopez; Lluis Asmarats; Manuel Pan; Jose Maria Novoa Medina; Juan Antonio Franco-Pelaez; Carlos Cuellas; Jessica Roa-Garrido; Maria Tamargo; Gabriela Veiga; Marta Herrero-Brocal; Pablo Miguel Valentin Garcia; Juan Garcia-Lara; Javier Cuesta; Felix Valencia-Serrano; Raquel Pimienta-Gonzalez; Jose Antonio Linares Vicente; Jorge Palazuelos-Molinero; Ivan Gomez-Blazquez; Josep Navarro-Manchon; Andrea Di Marco; Luis Garnacho-Gomez; Paula Vela-Martin; Cristina Martin-Arriscado; Fernando Sarnago Cebada
abstract:
Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP).
This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.
Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months.
In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups.
In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.
authors: Gijs M Broeze; Hugo M Aarts; Johanna da Silva Voorham; Kimberley I Hemelrijk; Dirk Jan van Ginkel; Geert A A Versteeg; Maik J Grundeken; Bimmer E P M Claessen; Pim A L Tonino; Carl E Schotborgh; Martijn Meuwissen; Gert K van Houwelingen; Joanna J Wykrzykowska; Giovanni Amoroso; Tessel N Vossenberg; Pieter A Vriesendorp; Niels van Royen; Jurriën M Ten Berg; Jan G P Tijssen; Michiel Voskuil; Ronak Delewi; PRO-TAVI Investigators
abstract:
Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies.
The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR.
This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed.
The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups.
In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
authors: Ramya C Mosarla; Binita Shah; Sunil V Rao; Sripal Bangalore; Pratik Manandhar; Leo Brothers; Jennifer Rymer; Nathaniel R Smilowitz
abstract:
Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown.
This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI.
Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified.
A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA.
IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

title: Validating ECG-Based Artificial Intelligence Models for Cardiomyopathy Detection in Obstetric Patients: A Multisite International Study.
authors: Demilade Adedinsewo; Patrick W Johnson; Carolina Morales-Lara; Maria Vitoria Coutinho; Sabrina D Phillips; Marc A Eidelhoch; Michal Cohen-Shelly; Elad Maor; Ariel Furer; Abraham Tsur; Shali Mazaki-Tovi; Kamilu M Karaye; Bosede Bukola Afolabi; Olusoji Edward Jagun; Sadiq Hassan Ringim; Kehinde Femi Ibiyemi; Okechukwu Samuel Ogah; Sabha Bhatti; Shakeela Naz; Haleema Yasmin; Maedeh Ganji; Jose Ruiz; Khadeeja Esmail; Jason Wheatley; Anekwe Onwuanyi; Eric Chang; Myah M Griffin; Oludamilola Oluleye; Stefanie Gefroh; Mohan Krishna Ranganathan; Samir Awasthi; Yvonne Butler Tobah; Francisco Lopez-Jimenez; Zachi I Attia; Paul A Friedman; Peter A Noseworthy; Rickey E Carter
abstract:
Cardiomyopathy significantly impacts maternal health worldwide. Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiograms (AI-ECG) have shown effectiveness in detecting left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) in adults and limited obstetric cohorts; however, broad validation in diverse obstetric populations remains unexplored.
Our primary objective was to validate the performance of 2 versions of an AI-ECG model for detecting cardiomyopathy in an international obstetric cohort.
We conducted a retrospective, multisite study of pregnant or postpartum women (≤12 months) across 11 institutions in 4 countries (Israel, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the United States). Two AI-ECG models (Food and Drug Administration-cleared v2.5.0 and refined v3.0.0) were evaluated against echocardiography. LVSD was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40% in keeping with the model's training target. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
We included 1,820 women with paired ECG-echocardiogram data, of whom 7.3% had LVSD. Model 1 (v2.5.0) demonstrated strong discriminative performance with an AUROC of 0.865, sensitivity of 46.1%, and negative predictive value of 95.8%. Model 2 (v3.0.0) showed significantly improved performance, with an AUROC of 0.925, sensitivity of 64.1%, and negative predictive value of 97.2% (P < 0.001) for LVSD detection.
AI-ECG models demonstrated strong external validity in a global obstetric cohort, with significantly improved performance in the refined model trained on expanded data. These findings support the potential role of AI-ECG for a scalable LVSD screening tool in obstetric populations, while underscoring the importance of population-specific validation prior to clinical implementation.

authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.
