title: A data-driven framework to identify restenosis-prone regions in femoral arteries from geometric and inflow waveform parameters
authors: Chotirawee Chatpattanasiri; Federica Ninno; Vanessa Díaz‐Zuccarini; Stavroula Balabani
journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
abstract: Haemodynamic indices derived from computational fluid dynamics (CFD), such as time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS) and oscillatory shear index (OSI), are closely associated with restenosis risk in peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We present a machine learning-reduced order modelling (ML-ROM) framework to predict critical, restenosis-prone, haemodynamic regions accounting for both vessel geometries and inlet flow waveforms. We generated 500 parameterized virtual femoral-artery geometries, each paired with a synthetic physiologically realistic inflow waveform. CFD was used to obtain the wall shear stress (WSS) distribution, from which TAWSS and OSI were computed. Critical regions were then defined by applying different thresholding criteria based on TAWSS and OSI, as found in the literature. These were then used to construct ROMs using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), and to train ML models from which the critical regions could be reconstructed. Four ML architectures were explored: a geometric-parameter-only model and three alternatives that also incorporate inflow waveform information via Fourier coefficients, long short-term memory (LSTM), and convolutional neural networks (CNN). The Fourier models achieved the highest predictive performance, with the median values of balanced accuracy (BA) exceeding 0.92 across all critical-region definitions. The model also offered a substantial speed-up ratio of the order of 109 compared with traditional CFD.

title: Multidimensional Echocardiographic Parameters Predict Left Ventricular Functional Recovery After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting
authors: Man Zhang; Jun Xia; Xiaoling Wan; Xuejiao Chen
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of preoperative and early postoperative echocardiographic parameters for left ventricular function recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to evaluate the relationship between functional recovery and 1-year clinical prognosis.METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 214 patients undergoing first-time elective CABG at The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University between January 2022 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, 3–7 days postoperatively, and at 6 months to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial volume index (LAVI), and ratio of early mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e′). Based on 6‑month LVEF change, patients were divided into recovery (ΔLVEF ≥5%) and non‑recovery (ΔLVEF <5%) groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and the corresponding models were established and validated. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded at 1‑year follow‑up.RESULTS: Of the 214 patients enrolled in the study, functional recovery of the left ventricle was observed in 128 individuals, corresponding to 59.8% of the cohort. Multivariate analysis identified several preoperative and procedural variables as independent predictors of functional recovery, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left atrial diameter (LAD), Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score, and the number of graft vessels. Age, preoperative LVEF, and e′ velocity were independently associated with lower odds of functional recovery. Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diabetes history showed no independent predictive value. The clinical-echocardiographic combined model demonstrated excellent discrimination and showed higher discriminative performance than the basic clinical model and conventional echocardiographic model. Subgroup analysis revealed that GLS showed no independent predictive value across all LVEF subgroups (p > 0.05), whereas LAVI and LAD were significant predictors in patients with LVEF ≥40% (including the 40%–49% subgroup), but showed no predictive relevance in those with LVEF <40%. Early postoperative ΔLVEF predicted 6-month functional recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.846. After one year of follow‑up, the recovery group exhibited a markedly lower rate of MACE than the non‑recovery group, with left ventricular functional recovery serving as an independent protective factor against MACE.CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative structural parameters, including LAVI, LVEDD, LVESD, and LAD, are independent imaging biomarkers for predicting left ventricular functional recovery after CABG. GLS and E/e′ ratio show no independent predictive value in this study. The integrated model combining clinical factors with multi-dimensional echocardiographic parameters demonstrates excellent discriminative ability. Early postoperative LVEF improvement strongly predicts 6-month functional recovery, while postoperative recovery of left ventricular function is associated with a significantly lower 1-year MACE risk.

title: External validation of the D-PACE score for predicting late high-grade atrioventricular block after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a Colombian cohort
authors: Juan David Zuluaga-Monroy; Hugo Oswaldo Alvarado Mora; Diana Fernanda Bohorquez Gonzalez; J.J. Sierra; Edgar Fernando Hurtado Ordoñez
abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries a clinically significant risk of late high-grade atrioventricular block (AVB), yet no validated tool exists to predict this complication in Latin-American populations. The D-PACE score was developed in European cohorts for this purpose. Methods In a retrospective cohort of 175 consecutive TAVR procedures at a Colombian center (2012–2025), 141 patients met inclusion criteria for D-PACE validation. The primary outcome was late high-grade AVB (≥Mobitz type II) occurring between 24 h and 30 days post-TAVR. Discrimination, logistic-regression calibration, and decision curve analysis were performed. Results Late AVB occurred in 31 patients (22.0%), with 80.6% of events within 72 h. The D-PACE score demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71–0.92; sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 86.4% at a cutoff of 5.5 points; NPV 93.1%). Late AVB rates rose progressively across strata: 5.9% (low-risk, score 0–3), 8.8% (intermediate, 4–5), and 61.5% (high-risk, ≥6), with the high-risk group concentrating 77.4% of all events. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities from 8% to 60%. All four low-risk events occurred among valve-in-valve patients assigned a score of 0 per the original algorithm; excluding this subgroup ( N = 114), the AUC rose to 0.91 (95% CI 0.85–0.96) with zero low-risk events. In an exploratory analysis applying the full seven-variable scoring uniformly, including valve-in-valve cases, the AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.85–0.95; NPV 96.7%), and 0.91 (95% CI 0.78–1.00) within the valve-in-valve subgroup ( N = 27, 4 events). Conclusions Applied as originally specified, the D-PACE score showed good discrimination for late high-grade AVB in this cohort (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71–0.92). The algorithm's automatic low-risk classification of valve-in-valve patients was not supported (14.8% AVB rate). Discrimination was higher both in the sensitivity analysis excluding valve-in-valve cases and in the exploratory analysis applying the seven-variable scoring uniformly, indicating that the scoring variables transfer well while the valve-in-valve exemption warrants reconsideration. These findings provide the first external validation of D-PACE in Latin America.

title: A novel LARP7 variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways
authors: Mozan Hassan; Manal Irshaid; Aalia Batool; Wadima Ali; Latifa Ba Qehaizel; Shamma Alzaabi; Shamma AlNuaimi; Sara Saeed; Fatma Al Jasmi; Nadia A. Akawi
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Background LARP7 encodes a critical scaffold protein of the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK snRNP) complex that regulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LARP7 cause Alazami syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, growth restriction, and distinctive craniofacial features. However, the transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency in human cells remain poorly understood, and the phenotypic spectrum of the disorder is incompletely defined. Methods We investigated a 6-year-old boy with clinically diagnosed Alazami syndrome who carried a novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant. Clinical evaluation and exome sequencing of blood-derived genomic DNA were performed, while quantitative PCR, Western blotting, and transcriptomic analysis were conducted using patient-derived dermal fibroblasts. Transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency were assessed by RNA sequencing, followed by single-subject differential expression, pathway enrichment, and network analyses. Results The patient presented with classical features of Alazami syndrome and tetralogy of Fallot, a cardiac manifestation not previously reported in the disorder. The novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant resulted in marked depletion of LARP7 transcripts and complete loss of full-length protein. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 1,224 dysregulated genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, developmental remodeling, cell-cycle regulation, and immune signaling. Pathway and network analyses highlighted dysregulation of STAT3-associated signaling together with SMAD3-linked extracellular matrix and developmental programs, identifying candidate developmental and tissue-remodeling pathways that warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models. Conclusion This study provides the first comprehensive transcriptomic characterization of genetically confirmed LARP7 deficiency in primary human cells and potentially expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome. The findings reveal widespread dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways, offering new insight into the molecular basis of the multisystem manifestations of Alazami syndrome and providing a framework for future functional and genotype–phenotype studies.

title: Early and Long-Term Results of 101 Consecutive Patients After Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation
authors: Damian Hudziak; Monika Gruz-Kwapisz; Radosław Parma; Wojciech Wańha; Sylwia Gładysz-Wańha; Wojciech Wojakowski; Radosław Gocoł
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation through the common carotid artery (TC-TAVI) is one of the possible treatment options for patients with ineligible transfemoral approach. The aim of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patients treated with TC-TAVI in early and long-term follow-up. Methods: The study included patients with severe aortic stenosis treated with TC-TAVI. In-hospital outcomes, early, long-term follow-up were presented in accordance with the VARC-3 recommendations. Results: The analysis presented 101 patients. We observed high procedural success-97% (n = 98). The number of VARC-3 incidents: 3.96% major vascular complications; 0.99% myocardial infarction; 0.99% cardiac tamponade; 0.99% life-threatening bleeding; 3.96% cerebrovascular incidents. The NYHA class decreased significantly compared to the pre-procedure value (2 [1–2] vs. 3 [3–3]; p < 0.001). There was a significant improvement in postprocedural cerebral oximetry values compared to baseline on both the implanted and contralateral sides (67.5 [63–71]% vs. 70 [63.5–75]%; p < 0.05) and (67 [64–71]% vs. 71 [64–76]%; p < 0.05), respectively. The 30-day, 1-year, and 2-year survival rates were 94.1%, 80.2%, and 69.3%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, BAV (HR 4.54; 95% CI: 1.14–17.99; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 7.32; 95% CI: 2.59–20.65; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with two-year mortality. In an exploratory adjusted Cox regression analysis, BAV (HR 2.63; 95% CI: 1.07–6.45; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 3.48; 95% CI: 1.67–7.24; p < 0.001) were associated with higher 2-year mortality. Conclusions: Our single-center, observational report indicated feasibility and good observed outcomes of the TC-TAVI procedure in an experienced clinical team.

title: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair: case report and analysis of existing literature
authors: Loes H. Willems; Marcus Steinbach; Daniel Pink; Thomas Herold; Alexander J. Meyer; Roger Wahba
abstract: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy that may mimic common EVAR-related complications. We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive lower back pain and was initially suspected of having a graft infection. Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm. Biopsy confirmed aortic angiosarcoma. No regional lymph node or distant metastases were identified. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and docetaxel, followed by radiotherapy and surgical resection of the abdominal aorta and EVAR graft with aortic reconstruction. Histopathological examination demonstrated complete pathological response without evidence of residual angiosarcoma. Our literature review identified only 21 reported cases of abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following EVAR, including the present case, underscoring the exceptional rarity of this entity and the limited evidence available to guide diagnosis and treatment. This case highlights the importance of considering aortic angiosarcoma in patients with persistent symptoms and atypical periaortic findings after EVAR and suggests that early biopsy and a multidisciplinary, multimodal treatment approach may improve outcomes despite the generally poor prognosis associated with this disease.

title: Impact of Socioeconomic Status and Rurality on the Rate of Prenatal Detection of Major and Critical Congenital Heart Disease in Western Australia
authors: Steven Hurwitz; Elaine O'Connell; Bradley R. MacDonald; Darshan Kothari; Jan Elizabeth Dickinson; Deane Yim
journal: Journal of Paediatrics and Child Health
abstract: AIM: Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with reduced infant morbidity and mortality. Location and subsequent socioeconomic status influence rates and timing of prenatal diagnoses of CHD. We investigated the impact of socioeconomic status and rurality on the rate of prenatal diagnosis of critical and major CHD in Western Australia (WA). METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed all critical (surgical intervention ≤ 30 days of life) and major (surgical intervention ≤ 1 year of life) CHD in WA between 2017 and 2021. Patients were identified from the WA Fetal Cardiology and Perth Children's Hospital Cardiology Databases. Clinical records were used to identify diagnoses, outcomes, postcode, rurality (via the Modified Monash Model [MMM]) and socioeconomic status (Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas [SEIFA] Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Postcode was used to estimate SEIFA index and MMM rurality. RESULTS: There were 478 cases with major CHD; 282 (59%) were prenatally diagnosed, of which 268 cases were critical CHD, with a 77% detection rate. Seventy-four percent of patients were from metropolitan areas. The distribution of SEIFA decile (p = 0.15) and MMM (p = 0.09) were not significantly different between pre- and postnatal groups. The diagnosis rate of univentricular CHD was 94% (n = 102) and 49% (n = 180) for CHD undergoing biventricular repair. CONCLUSION: Critical CHD increases the likelihood of prenatal diagnosis in WA; however, rurality and socioeconomic status were not found to influence diagnosis rates. Further studies are needed to review the availability of obstetric services in rural communities to ensure equitable healthcare.

title: Scoring balloon versus plain balloon vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon angioplasty for femoropopliteal atherosclerotic occlusive disease: a two-centre retrospective cohort study
authors: Lei Qi; Hongzhi Sun; Yaying Wu; Yihao Wang; Jiannan Wang; Yizhan Shi; Zhijian Dai; Jiahe Zhang; Shuangshuang Li; Zan Zeng; Jian Zhou
abstract: Background Optimal vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty in femoropopliteal atherosclerotic occlusive disease remains counteracted by dissection and recoil. We evaluated whether scoring balloon (SB) vessel preparation improves procedural immediate effect and mid-term outcomes compared with plain balloon (PB). Methods Patients with femoropopliteal occlusive disease undergoing DCB angioplasty following SB or PB preparation (2022-2025) across two tertiary centers were reviewed. 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was implemented. Primary endpoint was target vessel dissection. Secondary endpoints included bailout stenting, procedural complications, ankle-brachial index (ABI), 12-month primary patency, and freedom from clinically driven target vessel revascularisation (CD-TVR). Results After matching, 63 patients were in each group. Target vessel dissection occurred in 49.2% of Group PB and 17.5% of Group SB (OR: 5.00, 95% CI: 1.91–13.06, p = 0.001). For Groups PB and SB, bailout stenting rates were 31.7% and 9.5%, respectively (OR: 3.80, 95% CI: 1.42–10.17; p = 0.008). Procedural complication rates were 6.3% and 3.2% (OR: 2.00, 95% CI: 0.37–10.92; p = 0.424). 12-month primary patency were 87.3% and 88.9% (HR: 1.18, 95% CI: 0.44–3.22; p = 0.739). 12-month freedom from CD-TVR were 88.9% and 93.7% (HR: 1.83, 95% CI: 0.52–6.47; p = 0.348). Conclusion In this propensity-matched cohort, SB vessel preparation before DCB angioplasty was associated with lower rates of target vessel dissection and bailout stenting than PB. No statistically significant difference in the prespecified procedural complications, 12-month patency or CD-TVR was observed.

title: Wearable Single-Lead ECG Detects Fine-Grained Structural Heart Disease Through Echo-Report Supervision
authors: Shenda Hong; Chao He; Qinghao Zhao; Shun Huang; Jun Li; Gongzheng Tang; Hao Zhang; Tong Liu; Zheng-Kai Xue; Jian Liu; Kangyin Chen; Cheng Ding

title: STK39 is associated with endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory activation under hypoxic conditions in moyamoya disease
authors: Rui Liang; Zhenyu Zhou; 張耀仁; Xun Ye; Youjia Tang; Shihao He; Yuanli Zhao
abstract: Objective Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a cerebrovascular disease whose mechanism relatively unknown and can cause vascular occlusion and hyperplasia. This study aimed to explore molecular heterogeneity associated with the expression of acetylation-related genes in MMD and to identify candidate genes potentially involved in vascular endothelial dysfunction. Methods Public MMD transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using a predefined acetylation-regulatory gene set to identify expression clusters and prioritize cluster-associated candidate genes. Functional enrichment, immune-infiltration, and predicted miRNA–mRNA network analyses were performed to characterize candidate-associated molecular features. Serum STK39 and MTMR12 concentrations were assessed by ELISA in a preliminary study of three patients with MMD and three healthy controls. STK39 was further investigated in human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) using siRNA-mediated knockdown under normoxic and hypoxic conditions, with Trichostatin A (TSA) treatment included as an exploratory pharmacological intervention. Results Consensus clustering was used to classify MMD into two subtypes, and five key subtype-related genes were identified: STK39, NEO1, PKNOX1, GOLT1B, and MTMR12. In the validation cohort, serum STK39 and MTMR12 levels were significantly decreased in patients with MMD. In vitro , STK39 knockdown promoted HBMEC migration, inhibited proliferation, and increased the expression of HIF-1α, p-STAT3, cleaved Caspase-3, IL-6, CCL2, and VCAM-1 under hypoxic conditions, whereas TSA treatment partially reversed these changes. Conclusion Acetylation-related genes are closely associated with the molecular heterogeneity of MMD. Among them, STK39 appears to participate in hypoxia-related endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory activation. These findings provide new insight into the role of acetylation-related pathways in MMD pathogenesis and suggest potential targets for future mechanistic studies.

title: Liveborn trisomy 22: a case report
authors: Sofia Jares Baglivo; Megan P. Morand; Gopalrao V.N. Velagaleti; Sunil K. Jain; Erin Cooney
abstract: Introduction : Trisomy 22 is identified in 2%–5% of spontaneous abortions across various populations, making it the second most common trisomy in spontaneous abortions. Liveborn patients with complete trisomy 22 are rare and present with variable clinical findings. Methods A detailed clinical report of a term female neonate with complete trisomy 22 was compiled after obtaining informed consent from her mother. Results The neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and resuscitation included intubation after multiple attempts. She presented with multiple congenital anomalies, including a single umbilical artery, microcephaly, dysmorphic facial features, absent red reflex, corneal haze, irregular pupil, microcornea, imperforated anus with rectovestibular fistula, bilateral clinodactyly of the fifth digits, and bilateral distal and proximal transverse palmar creases running parallel to each other. An echocardiogram showed Tetralogy of Fallot and hypoplasia of the transverse aortic arch. Abdominal ultrasound revealed small kidneys. The electroencephalogram showed diffuse cerebral dysfunction. Head ultrasound indicated absence of the septum pellucidum. Additional complications included pneumothorax, metabolic disturbances, sepsis, and persistent thrombocytopenia. The neonate's condition deteriorated, leading to demise on the seventh day of life. Chromosome analysis confirmed 47,XX,+22. Discussion : This case report contributes to the limited literature on complete trisomy 22, highlighting its prognosis, clinical heterogeneity, and management challenges. The constellation of anomalies observed underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and adaptability in providing optimal care. By better understanding its clinical presentation, we hope to facilitate early recognition, appropriate management, and counseling.

title: Severe dynamic left-ventricular outflow-tract obstruction unmasked by transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a case report
authors: Zongmei Gao; Minghui Yuan; Yi Li; Jingli Lu; Ruijian Li
abstract: Structured Abstract Background Relieving the fixed afterload of severe aortic stenosis can unmask a previously concealed dynamic outflow-tract obstruction. Case summary A 69-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.65 cm2; 109/64 mmHg), mild concentric hypertrophy (septum 15 mm) and no baseline systolic anterior motion (SAM) underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The invasive peak-to-peak gradient fell from 64 to 7 mmHg, but echocardiography immediately afterwards showed new SAM and severe dynamic left-ventricular-outflow-tract (LVOT) obstruction (170/67 mmHg) with hypotension. Treatment was load-directed (volume expansion, avoidance of vasodilators and inotropes, beta-blockade), with a cardiac myosin inhibitor as an adjunct. Over four months the resting LVOT gradient fell to 22/13 mmHg and the provoked peak to 29 mmHg, with SAM no longer seen and preserved ejection fraction. Discussion Recognising this load-dependent obstruction during the procedure and restoring loading, rather than escalating inotropes, is the key lesson.

title: Factors associated with short- and long-term maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful elective electrical cardioversion
authors: Nikola N. Radovanović; Nemanja S. Branković; N Vujadinovic; Nebojsa M Mujović; Stefan Juričić; Olga Petrovic; Srdjan Raspopović; Goran Milašinović
abstract: Introduction Electrical cardioversion (ECV) effectively restores sinus rhythm in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), although arrhythmia recurrence is common. We aimed to identify factors associated with a higher probability of maintaining sinus rhythm one month after successful ECV, and after one year in those who were arrhythmia-free after the first month. Methods This retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent elective ECV for persistent AF or AFL between January 2011 and June 2023. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic characteristics were analyzed to identify parameters associated with the maintenance of sinus rhythm. Results We included 297 ECV procedures. ECV was successful in 91.9% of patients and sinus rhythm was maintained in 89.7% of them at one month and in 40.3% at one year follow-up. Shorter arrhythmia duration (OR = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.76–0.98, p = 0.026) and ventricular pacing on the pre-procedural ECG (OR = 5.212, 95% CI: 1.16–23.48, p = 0.032) were associated with one-month success. Factors associated with one-year sinus rhythm maintenance in patients who were in sinus rhythm during monthly follow-up were smaller left atrial dimensions (OR = 0.817, 95%CI: 0.77–0.98, p = 0.022), the first-ever arrhythmia episode (OR = 3.320, 95%CI: 1.10–10.05, p = 0.034), lower CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score (OR = 0.132, 95%CI: 0.03–0.54, p = 0.005), non-smoking status (OR = 0.120, 95%CI: 0.04–0.37, p < 0.001), no previous ECV (OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.01–0.47, p = 0.005), and antiarrhythmic therapy (OR = 2.486, 95%CI: 1.01–8.65, p = 0.05). Conclusions ECV is a reasonable rhythm-control strategy in AF/AFL particularly when performed early after arrhythmia onset, in non-smokers and patients with fewer comorbidities, antiarrhythmic treatment, smaller left atrium and no prior ECV.

title: LP(a)-LOWERING THERAPIES (siRNA / ASO) AND ATHEROSCLEROTIC RISK REDUCTION
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Genetically determined and independent risk factor, High levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)].Traditional lipid-lowering drugs like statins and PCSK9 inhibitors are not effective enough to decrease the levels of Lp(a) and leave a considerable amount of cardiovascular risk.New RNA-based treatment approaches, such as small interfering RNA (siRNA) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), are currently appearing as the potential solutions, which can significantly reduce the levels of Lp(a) by acting on the expression of the hepatic LPA gene.The purpose of this study was to assess the professional attitudes to the safety, efficacy, and clinical relevance of Lp (a)-lowering RNA therapeutics and their role in reducing the risk of ASCVD.Methods: A cross-sectional survey was carried out quantitatively on cardiology, pharmacology, and molecular biology professionals.A 30-item Likert-scale questionnaire (1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree) was designed to gather the data and was given to 263 respondents.The data were analyzed through SPSS 26 in terms of Normality (Shapiro-Wilk), Reliability (Cronbach-alpha), and Validity (KMO and Bartlett's), Inferential Tests (t-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square).Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis were also done to test associations and predictive relationships between variables. Results:The distribution of all items was found to be normal (p > 0.05) and had a high reliability (0.978) and a high construct validity (KMO = 0.874, p = 0.001).There were also notable variations by gender, age, and education level (p < 0.05), and this demonstrates that demographic and professional variables have a role in perceptions of RNA-based lipid-lowering therapy.Correlation analysis showed that there were strong positive relationships between all variables (r = 0.680.88,p < 0.01).The significance of the regression model was (R 2 = 0.716, p = 0.001), which indicated that awareness, perceived efficacy, safety, and adoption intention had positive influences on attitudes toward risk reduction of ASCVD.Conclusion: The research supports the hypothesis that healthcare and biomedical professionals have a very favorable opinion of Lp(a)-lowering siRNA/ASO therapies as a safe and effective method of residual cardiovascular risk management.The statistical results indicate a high level of reliability, validity, and predictability, which attests to the high level of professional trust in RNA-based therapeutics.Such results justify the importance of genetic and molecular treatments in the future cardiovascular risk management systems, which would be a significant change towards precision lipidology and personalized medicine.

title: Bronchial Atresia Associated With a Giant Subpleural Bulla: A Case Report
authors: Carolina P Figueira; Helena Fragoeiro; Maria Cunha; Joana Lobato; Bruno F Couto; Mariana Passos e Sousa Marques Afonso
abstract: Bronchial atresia is a rare congenital malformation characterized by focal interruption of a lobar, segmental, or subsegmental bronchus, with distal mucus impaction and hyperinflation of the affected lung.It is usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally.We report the case of a 25-year-old man with no relevant medical history who presented to primary care with a three-day history of productive cough, rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, and myalgia.Physical examination revealed hyperresonance to percussion and markedly diminished breath sounds throughout the left hemithorax.Chest radiography showed marked left-sided hyperlucency with contralateral mediastinal shift.Chest computed tomography demonstrated a focal abnormality of the left upper lobe bronchus with distal mucus-filled bronchial dilatation consistent with a bronchocele, together with a giant subpleural bulla measuring approximately 25 cm along its longest axis and occupying about half of the left hemithorax.After multidisciplinary assessment, elective video-assisted thoracoscopic resection of the bulla was performed.The procedure was complicated by an iatrogenic laceration of the descending aorta during division of the inferior pulmonary ligament, causing major arterial hemorrhage and requiring emergent conversion to thoracotomy and direct aortic repair.The postoperative course was complicated by left pleural empyema, which was successfully treated with antibiotics and drainage.At three months, the patient reported only mild exertional dyspnea, with no recurrent respiratory infection or pneumothorax and satisfactory radiographic re-expansion of the remaining left lung.This case highlights an uncommon association between bronchial atresia and extensive bullous disease, the value of careful assessment of disproportionate physical findings, and the importance of individualized surgical planning when marked intrathoracic anatomical distortion is present.

title: Pulsed Electromagnetic Field Driven Perturbation of Peripheral Arterial Hemodynamics: Integrated Evidence from Doppler Ultrasound and Photoplethysmographic Signal Analysis
authors: Ahmed Kiser; Tarikul Islam; Jubair Ibn Omar Hamza; Sumaiya Tabassum Dipty; Syed Salman Aziz; Md. Mahbubur Rahman; Jamil Hasan Karami; Mohammad Rashal Chowdhury; Shahnaj Latif; Muhammad E. H. Chowdhury; K. Ayaz Rabbani; Zaid Bin Mahbub
abstract: Pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) have been widely studied for vascular and microcirculatory modulation, yet their effects on pulsatile hemodynamic organization remain poorly characterized. It is also unclear whether reversing field direction under otherwise comparable exposure conditions can alter vascular waveform behaviour. This study investigated acute direction-dependent responses to PEMF using Doppler ultrasound and photoplethysmography (PPG). Twenty healthy volunteers underwent PEMF exposure (10 Hz, 100 µs pulse width, 15 V) over the brachial artery with the coil in two opposing orientations, such that the local induced electric-field component along the arterial axis was directed either with (Forward) or against (Reverse) physiological blood flow. Downstream responses were assessed using radial artery Doppler and index-finger PPG. Participant-level feature summaries were analyzed using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, including direct comparison of baseline-corrected Forward and Reverse responses, complemented by descriptive kernel-density L1 (KDE-L1) analysis. PPG showed the clearest participant-level responses. Six Forward features involving temporal, morphological, and pulse-area characteristics remained FDR-significant (q =0.018-0.037), whereas five Reverse features involving systolic amplitude, notch timing, and spectral organization remained significant (q = 0.003-0.012). Direct Forward-Reverse comparison identified significant differences in eight PPG features spanning amplitude, area, temporal, and spectral domains (q =0.005-0.029). Doppler showed a more selective response, with Forward Cardiac Cycle Duration remaining FDR-significant (q= 0.014), together with broader KDE-L1 redistribution of arterial velocity-waveform characteristics. These findings demonstrate orientation-sensitive peripheral pulse-wave responses together with complementary arterial waveform changes, supporting field direction as a potentially relevant exposure parameter in vascular PEMF research.

title: Beyond the clinic: a six-month home-based exercise and respiratory rehabilitation program improves functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue in chronic heart failure
authors: Mariusz Ciołkiewicz; Mariusz Wojciuk; Anna Kuryliszyn-Moskal; Agnieszka Dakowicz; Emilia Sawicka; Karol Adam Kamiński
abstract: Introduction Optimal models of rehabilitation dedicated for patients with heart failure (HF) remain under investigation. The aim of this study was to assess the safety and effectiveness of a 6-month home-based rehabilitation program in patients with HF. Materials and methods 63 patients with stable HF were randomized, 28 patients from intervention group completed the study and were included in the analysis. Assessments including the 6-minute walk test, respiratory muscle strength, and quality of life measures (SF-36 and Fatigue Severity Scale – FSS) were conducted at baseline and after 6 months. Additionally, adverse events and adherence to the training protocol were monitored. Results Due to objective challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, the course and final outcomes of the study differed from the original protocol; the control group was not assessed after 6 months. In the intervention group, 6 months of rehabilitation resulted in statistically significant improvements: the 6-minute walk distance increased by 37.86 meters ( p = 0.001), maximal inspiratory pressure (PImax) improved by 20.21 cmH₂O, and maximal expiratory pressure (PEmax) by 20.75 cmH₂O (both p < 0.01). A significant reduction in fatigue was observed, as measured by FSS, with a mean decrease of 0.68 points ( p = 0.029). Adherence to the exercise protocol averaged 91.5 ± 15.3%. No serious adverse events were reported. Conclusions The home-based rehabilitation program, including respiratory muscle training, is safe and effective for patients with chronic HF. It improves functional capacity and reduces fatigue levels. Clinical Trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03780803 , ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03780803. Registered 19/12/2018.

title: VARIATIONS IN BRANCHING PATTERN OF THE LEFT CORONARY ARTERY AND CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF TRIANGLE OF BROCQ AND MOUCHET: CADAVERIC STUDY
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: The left coronary artery (LCA) shows marked anatomical variability in its branching pattern, which is crucial for interventional and surgical procedures.The Triangle of Brocq and Mouchet (TBM), formed by the left anterior descending artery (LAD), left circumflex artery (LCx), and great cardiac vein (GCV), is a key yet under-explored coronary landmark with clinical and radiological significance.Methods: Thirty human cadaveric hearts from routine dissections were studied to document LCA origin, branching patterns, and TBM morphology.The LCA was classified as bifurcating, trifurcating, quadrifurcating, or pentafurcating.The TBM was evaluated for its presence, completeness, shape, and contents.The positional relationship of the GCV with the LAD and LCx was also assessed.Results: TBM was present in all specimens, predominantly in a closed form (80%), followed by inferiorly (10%) and superiorly (10%) open types.The triangle commonly contained a median artery (36.7%), diagonal branch (26.7%), or both (6.7%); one specimen showed a GCV tributary.LCA branching patterns included bifurcation (50%), trifurcation (20%), quadrifurcation (20%), and pentafurcation (10%).The GCV was superficial to the LAD in 33.3% and deep in 66.7%, while superficial to the LCx in 60% and deep in 40% of cases.Conclusion: This study highlights notable variability in LCA branching and TBM configuration, with the closed triangle being most common.Awareness of these variations is essential during coronary interventions and bypass grafting to prevent iatrogenic injury and improve procedural accuracy.

title: Evaluation of mitral regurgitation severity in type 1 acute myocardial infarction: correlation with wall motion score index and infarct location
authors: Irine Ferza Sulfiker; Shalaka S Ramgir; Shreeyash Tulpule; Sammita Jadhav

title: Endoscopic secondary chordae transfer and edge-to-edge repair for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse
abstract: Anterior leaflet prolapse remains a challenging lesion in mitral valve repair, particularly in the presence of asymmetric degenerative disease. We present the case of a 59-year-old patient with severe mitral regurgitation due to asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse in the setting of Barlow’s disease, treated through a totally endoscopic right minithoracotomy. Intraoperative valve analysis demonstrated prolapse of the A2M2 and A3 segments with elongated secondary chordae. Mitral valve repair was performed using secondary chordae transfer, followed by asymmetric edge-to-edge repair at the A2–P2 scallops and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative assessment showed satisfactory leaflet coaptation with trivial residual regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed the absence of residual mitral regurgitation and no evidence of clinically significant mitral stenosis. This report describes the technical aspects of endoscopic secondary chordae transfer combined with asymmetric edge-to-edge repair and ring annuloplasty for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse, demonstrating the feasibility of this repair strategy in a complex mitral valve anatomy.

title: Case Report: Discordant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in monozygotic twins with LEOPARD syndrome and an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation
authors: Xin Xue; Yayuan Ning; Fang Yao; Xiaowei Zhang; Xianjing Song
abstract: LEOPARD syndrome (LS; Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines) is a rare autosomal dominant RASopathy in which PTPN11 mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with highly variable expressivity. We report adolescent monozygotic twin brothers carrying an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation that arose de novo , who developed discordant cardiac phenotypes despite sharing a genome and an intrauterine and postnatal environment. The younger twin developed obstructive HCM with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (peak resting gradient 36 mmHg, peak Valsalva gradient 61 mmHg), together with pectus excavatum and macroglossia; the older twin had non-obstructive HCM (maximal septal thickness 12 mm) with a patent foramen ovale. Both twins had multiple lentigines, facial dysmorphism, and sensorineural hearing loss requiring cochlear implantation. The younger twin was treated with a beta-blocker and activity restriction, whereas the older twin was managed with surveillance alone. This case demonstrates that an identical RASopathy mutation can produce divergent forms of HCM, supports a role for non-genetic modifiers in cardiovascular expression, and underscores the need for hemodynamics-guided, individualized cardiovascular management in LS.

title: The correlation between epicardial adipose tissue thickness and left ventricular systolic function in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus
authors: Sisi Lin; Shengmin Zhang; Hui Zhou
abstract: Background Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can cause myocardial damage and left ventricular dysfunction in patients. Abnormal deposition of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) can promote the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate changes in EAT thickness in patients with SLE and apply two-dimensional speckle tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) to study the correlation between EAT and left ventricular systolic function. Patients and methods This case–control study recruited a total of 67 SLE patients as the case group and 31 healthy individuals as the control group. Left ventricular systolic function parameters were measured using 2D-STE. Changes and correlations in laboratory indicators, EAT, and left ventricular systolic function parameters were compared between groups. Results Compared with the control group, the case group showed significantly increased EAT and diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWD) ( P <0.05). High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (AP2C LS), apical three-chamber longitudinal strain (AP3C LS), apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (AP4C LS), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were significantly reduced ( P < 0.05). The 18-segment left ventricular longitudinal strain was further grouped according to coronary artery supply; the LAD, RCA, and LCX groups in the patient cohort all showed reductions compared with the healthy control group ( P < 0.05). Spearman correlation analysis revealed that EAT was negatively correlated with GLS ( r = −0.39, P < 0.05), LAD group ( r = −0.26, P < 0.05), RCA group ( r = −0.47, P < 0.05), and LCX group ( r = −0.29, P < 0.05), and positively correlated with duration of illness (DT) ( r = 0.41, P < 0.05) and age ( r = 0.45, P < 0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis confirmed that EAT is an important influencing factor of left ventricular longitudinal strain function ( P < 0.05). Conclusion Increased epicardial adipose tissue thickness is negatively correlated with left ventricular systolic function. EAT can effectively reflect changes in left ventricular systolic function in SLE patients, providing a basis for clinical management and early intervention.

title: A Rare Presentation of Pneumococcal Meningitis with Acute Bilateral Vision Loss: A Case Report
authors: Adam Anderson; Alexander Piszker; Eric Applebach; Reid Mitchell; Aji Yagou Jeng
journal: Clinical Practice and Cases in Emergency Medicine
abstract: Introduction: Bacterial meningitis affects about 1.2 million people worldwide each year. Streptococcus pneumoniae is responsible for the majority of cases of bacterial meningitis in the United States and Europe, with visual impairment seen in 6.3% of patients. The etiology of acute vision loss in the setting of bacterial meningitis remains wide-ranging, most often occurring in the setting of endogenous endophthalmitis, optic neuropathy, and cortical blindness. Retinal necrosis is rare, and typically associated with viral meningitis, but has not been reported in bacterial meningitis. Case report: A 66-year-old man with headache, malaise, and intermittent blurry vision, initially diagnosed with viral upper respiratory infection and presumed trigeminal neuralgia, presented to the emergency department with altered mental status, meningismus, and progressive bilateral vision loss. He was diagnosed with bacterial meningitis, and subsequent cerebrospinal fluid and blood cultures were positive for S pneumoniae. Ophthalmologic evaluation demonstrated bilateral nonreactive pupils, retinal ischemia, optic nerve pallor, and retinal necrosis but no intraocular inflammation. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed multifocal cortical ischemic infarcts thought to be of embolic source. His hospitalization was complicated by mitral valve regurgitation, endocarditis, and cardiac tamponade requiring extensive surgical repair. Conclusion: This case represents a rare presentation of bilateral retinal ischemia and necrosis in the setting of S pneumoniae meningitis without evidence of endophthalmitis. Awareness of atypical ocular presentations and differential diagnoses is vital in providing early diagnosis, treatment and specialist involvement.

title: Progression of Tricuspid Regurgitation After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation and Its Impact on Mortality and Hospitalization: A Single‐Center Cohort Study
authors: Ahmet Can Urgancı; Filiz Özerkan Çakan; Evrim Şimşek
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) progression is a recognized complication of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation, yet its prognostic impact on long-term clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, 303 patients undergoing CIED implantation between 2005 and 2023 were followed for a median of 4.8 years. TR severity was assessed echocardiographically at baseline and 12 months. The primary endpoint was TR progression (≥ 1-grade worsening); secondary endpoints were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular hospitalization, their composite, and progression to severe TR, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. TR progressed in 103 patients (34.0%), regressed in 33 (10.9%), and remained stable in 167 (55.1%), a net rightward shift (p < 0.001). Progression differed by device type (p = 0.031): among the larger subgroups, VVI-ICD showed the greatest net progression (31.8% worsened vs. 6.9% improved; p < 0.001) and CRT-D the highest regression (18.8%). During follow-up, 67 patients (22.1%) died and 164 (54.1%) were hospitalized. Overall TR progression was not independently associated with mortality (HR 1.118, p = 0.693) but independently predicted cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 1.640, p = 0.003) and the composite endpoint (HR 1.480, p = 0.014). On unadjusted analysis, progression specifically to severe TR (n = 15) was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.99, p = 0.024) and cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 2.45, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: TR progression occurs in approximately one-third of CIED recipients within the first year and independently predicts cardiovascular hospitalization. Progression to severe TR identifies a higher-risk subset, supporting routine post-implant echocardiographic surveillance.

title: Association between the inferior vena cava collapsibility index and Fontan pressure in patients with Fontan physiology: a two-centre prospective pilot study
authors: Matthew D. Campbell; Arshid M. Mir; Shashank Behere; Jennifer H. Huang; Grant Burch; Mohammad Alnoor; Erin Madriago
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with functional single ventricle anatomy undergo staged surgical palliation in early childhood culminating in the Fontan procedure whereby the inferior vena cava is connected to the pulmonary artery. Fontan circulation inherently requires elevated central venous pressure to maintain adequate pulmonary blood flow; however, excessive elevation is associated with morbidity and mortality. In adults, a key component of echocardiographic evaluation is the use of a "sniff test" as a surrogate of downstream right atrial pressure. This technique has not yet been validated as a measure of pressure assessment in patients with Fontan circulation. METHODS: This was a two-center prospective study of patients with functional single ventricle physiology who had undergone the Fontan procedure and were undergoing previously scheduled transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac catheterization as part of their standard clinical care. We correlated collapsibility index on echocardiogram with directly obtained Fontan pressure measurements from cardiac catheterization performed the same day. RESULTS: 15 patients were enrolled and analyzed for the study. Collapsibility index demonstrated an inverse correlation with Fontan pressure, (Pearson r = -0.72, R2 = 0.51, p = 0.003). Collapsibility index was significantly higher for patients with non-elevated Fontan pressure (45% vs 30%, p = 0.0005). Using a collapsibility index threshold of 35.0% demonstrated a 100% positive predictive value for detecting elevated Fontan pressure (greater than 14 mmHg). CONCLUSIONS: There was a significant inverse relationship between the collapsibility index and Fontan pressure. These findings may suggest a possible association between collapsibility index and Fontan pressure, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
authors: Laurenz Hauptmann; Christina Kronberger; Stéphanie Kristina Schwarting; Daniela Tomasoni; Lara S. Schlender; Sophia Koschatko; Maximilian Autherith; Charlotte Jantsch; Caglayan Demirel; Franz Duca; Andreas Anselm Kammerlander; Luca Bordignon; Gabriele Guidi Colombi; Nora Schwegel; Matteo Serenelli; Aldostefano Porcari; Steven A. Muller; Nicolas Verheyen; Marish I.F.J. Oerlemans; Μαρία Παπαθανασίου; Christian Hengstenberg; Marco Merlo; Jörg Hausleiter; Marianna Adamo; Philipp Emanuel Bartko; Christian Nitsche
abstract: BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. RESULTS: , regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study
authors: Gerhard Wess; Jens Häggström; Julia Stadler; Lara König; Katarzyna Kraszewska; Doris Bittenecker; Oriol Domènech; German Santamarina; Gregory Van den Noortgate; Mikkel Brandt Bjerknæs; Jenny Eberhard; Karin Kriström; Liva Vatne; Michał Gajewski; Christel Schinner-Peters; Guy Tater; Marin Torti; Christoph Schummer; Ingrid Ljungvall
abstract: Background Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Methods This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM. Results Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage ( p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6–46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages ( p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase. Conclusion Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

title: Turning the tide in heart failure: A case report of one-year improvement in a CRT-P super-responder with HFrEF and LBBB
authors: Fitri Febrianti Ramadhan; Ardian Rizal; Wella Karolina
abstract: Background: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is an established treatment for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and electrical dyssynchrony, especially in patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). In symptomatic patients with LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm and LBBB with a QRS duration ≥130 ms despite optimal treatment, CRT is suggested according to the 2021 ESC Guidelines to enhance symptoms, quality of life, and survival. In older patients who are not candidates for a defibrillator, cardiac resynchronization therapy pacemaker (CRT-P) is generally used. Response rates are generally 55% to 70% in large trials, with optimal outcomes in patients with LBBB and QRS duration ≥150 ms. Case Presentations: A 76-year-old woman physician with hypertension and dyslipidaemia, despite optimal treatment, presented with NYHA class III. ECG revealed complete LBBB in sinus rhythm. Echocardiography demonstrated an LVEF of 28%, left ventricular dilation, and significant functional mitral regurgitation. Coronary angiography was negative for obstructive coronary artery disease. CRT-P was implanted. At 6 months, the patient was still a non-responder with persistent systolic dysfunction, adverse remodelling, diastolic dysfunction and residual regurgitation. Echocardiography-guided device optimization adjusting AV delay by transmitral Doppler to preserve atrial contribution, VV delay by LVOT VTI and strain analysis to improve synchronization and reduce regurgitation. At One-year follow-up, the patient showed significant improvement in NYHA class I–II and improved exercise tolerance. Echocardiography showed significant reverse remodelling, and LVEF was improved to 67%. Device interrogation revealed ongoing thresholds and >99% biventricular pacing. Conclusions: This case illustrates a CRT-P super-responder outcome, the role of guideline-directed selection, close follow-up, and tailored optimization to maximize both clinical and structural benefits. Keyword : Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy; Cardiac Pacing; Heart Failure; Left Bundle Branch Block.

title: Histotripsy in tumor therapy: advances in non-thermal mechanical ablation, immune modulation, and clinical translation
authors: Yangyang Ma; Xinan Long; Jiangpeng Cheng; Lizhi Niu
abstract: Histotripsy is an emerging non-invasive focused-ultrasound technology that mechanically disrupts tissue through controlled bubble activity rather than sustained thermal coagulation. This review distinguishes shock-scattering cavitational histotripsy, intrinsic threshold histotripsy, and boiling histotripsy and relates their pulse regimes, bubble dynamics, tissue effects, monitoring strategies, and evidence maturity. Mechanical fractionation can expose tumor antigens and damage-associated molecular patterns, but immune outcomes vary by submodality, dose, tumor model, treated fraction, and sampling time; no standardized head-to-head evidence establishes a superior immunological approach. Early prospective liver studies demonstrate high technical feasibility and encouraging local control, whereas post-market cohorts also reveal targeting limitations and uncommon but clinically important vascular, thrombotic, and renal complications. Pancreatic investigation remains ongoing, while the renal CAIN study is completed with registry results and a peer-reviewed first-patient report. A clinically useful dosimetry framework should connect delivered acoustic parameters with in situ cavitation, tissue disruption, imaging or acoustic surrogates, and delayed oncologic and immune endpoints. Histotripsy should currently be viewed as a complementary local therapy with a distinctive mechanical mechanism rather than as a proven replacement for established ablation. Standardized reporting, independently adjudicated safety data, and prospective comparative trials are needed to define its durable oncologic and immunological value.

title: Selective conduction differences in children with isolated bicuspid aortic valve
authors: Uğur Saraç; Ayşe Büşra Paydaş; Mehmet Babür; Mehmet Burhan Oflaz; Tamer Baysal; Fatih Şap
abstract: Objective: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is one of the most common congenital heart defects, yet the electrocardiographic features of isolated BAV in children have not been well characterized. We aimed to evaluate electrocardiographic parameters in pediatric patients with isolated BAV and to investigate whether early electrical changes are detectable before overt valve dysfunction. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective case-control study, 30 children with isolated and hemodynamically uncomplicated BAV were compared with 32 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Via 12-lead surface electrocardiography, P wave parameters, QT and QTc intervals, QRS duration, axis measurements, and the QRS-T angle were assessed by two blinded investigators. For the ECG parameters, correction for multiple comparisons was applied with the Benjamini-Hochberg method. Results: The study included 30 children with BAV and 32 controls; median age was 142.5 versus 141.5 months, and male sex was present in 70.0% versus 75.0%, respectively. After correction for multiple comparisons, only the minimum duration of the P wave (q=0.005) and the dispersion of the P wave (q=0.008) showed significant differences between the groups; P minimum duration was higher and P wave dispersion was lower in the BAV group. No difference was found between the groups in the PR interval, QRS duration, the parameters of repolarization, and axis measurements. In the BAV group, aortic Z-scores were higher despite preserved systolic function of the left ventricle, and the left ventricular mass index did not reach statistical significance (p=0.058). Conclusion: Isolated pediatric BAV is associated with selective electrocardiographic changes at the level of atrial conduction, in the absence of a hemodynamic burden, while ventricular conduction and repolarization are not affected at this stage.

title: Antecedents and consequences of Green-tech FDI in emerging markets
authors: Zhuoran Liu
abstract: As environmental pressures intensify, attracting sustainable foreign direct investment (FDI), particularly green-tech FDI, has become a critical pathway for emerging markets to achieve environmental sustainability. However, existing research remains fragmented, offering limited insights into why green-tech FDI enters emerging markets and how it affects regional green innovation. This thesis addresses these gaps by systematically examining both the antecedents and consequences of green-tech FDI through three empirical studies using regional data from China. Study 1 and Study 2 focus on the antecedents of green-tech FDI. Study 1 examines how host-country conditions can attract green-tech FDI, highlighting the role of environmental management information disclosure (EMID) by domestic firms in reducing information gaps and strengthening green market–seeking motives. Study 2 shifts attention to the active decision-making of green-tech FDI, showing that under uncertainty, green-tech foreign investors engage in identity-based bandwagon learning by imitating peers with similar green identities, thereby mitigating investment risks. Study 3 turns to the consequences of green-tech FDI. It demonstrates that, due to the technological complexity of green innovation and limited absorptive capacity in emerging markets, green-tech FDI may generate crowding-out effects rather than purely positive spillovers. Adopting a network perspective, the study further finds that universities play a key moderating role: through broad linkages and deep collaborations, they help mitigate negative spillovers and facilitate the diffusion of green technologies. Together, the three studies advance the literature on sustainable FDI by differentiating green-tech FDI from general FDI and identifying the specific mechanisms that shape its entry decisions and local innovation outcomes. Practically, the findings provide guidance for emerging-market governments and firms on how to attract and manage sustainable investment, balance growth with environmental objectives, and strengthen local innovation ecosystems.

title: Combating Data and Target Shifts in Visual Tasks
authors: Zhaorui Tan
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning models for visual tasks has led to significant progress in many domains. However, a key challenge remains: ensuring that models can generalize effectively to unseen samples or novel classes, especially in real-world scenarios where training data-target pairs are often limited or unavailable, and test data may exhibit shifts in both data and targets. This thesis addresses the problem of shifts across data and targets, proposing novel methods to improve model generalization and transferability in complex settings. The thesis identifies the different shift scenarios for visual tasks and presents their problem forms. The research first relaxes the static target distribution assumption in Multi-Domain Generalization (mDG) tasks, introducing the General Multi-Domain Generalization (GMDG) objective to improve generalization under varying data shifts. Specifically, Extensive experiments validate that GMDG is feasible for classification, segmentation, and regression tasks. Further considering extreme target distribution shifts where even unknown novel classes emerge, the study also explores logical regularization techniques for tasks such as Generalized Category Discovery (GCD), mDG+GCD, and Class Incremental Learning (CIL), proposing a sample-based logical regularization term (L-Reg) to enhance data-, target-, and all-shift generalization. Additionally, a partial logic framework is introduced to address challenges in CIL, enabling models to retain room for unknown classes during training. This is further extended by the Partial-Logic Regularization (PL-Reg), which improves generalization across GCD, mDG+GCD, and transferability for CIL tasks. Furthermore, the thesis proposes a novel Semantic-aware Data Augmentation (SADA) framework for cross-modality generalization in text-to-image synthesis (T2Isyn), text-image retrieval (TIR), and image-text retrieval (ITR) tasks. This framework ensures semantic preservation across text and image modalities, improving both semantic consistency and image quality in cross-modality tasks. The methods proposed in this thesis offer significant advancements in visual generalization and transfer scenarios, providing theoretical insights and practical solutions for handling data shifts, target shifts, and multi-modalities in complex scenarios. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, demonstrating their superior performance across a range of tasks.

title: Depth of Processing, learner aptitude, and the acquisition of L2 English grammatical structures
authors: Shweta Nigam
abstract: Depth of Processing (DoP) is central to several models of instructed second language acquisition (ISLA) (Leow, 2015). While DoP has been extensively examined in vocabulary learning (e.g., Laufer & Hulstijn, 2001), its role in the acquisition of grammatical structures, particularly through oral and audio-visual modalities remains comparatively underexplored. Drawing on the Levels of Processing framework (Craik & Lockhart, 1972), this study investigated whether task-induced processing depth influences the acquisition of third conditionals and comparatives, and whether language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) predicts learning gains. Using a pretest–posttest design, four intact classes involving 108 Grade 8 EFL learners in India were assigned to one of the three experimental conditions differing in level and type of processing: Low DoP, High DoP Explicit, and High DoP Implicit. The treatment task required the participants to listen to an audio-visual story containing the target structures (third conditionals and comparatives) and complete analytic tasks (varying in different groups) before listening to the story for a second time. The oral performance of the participants was analysed for accuracy, and frequency of use of the target structures. A grammaticality judgement test (GJT) and an elicited imitation task (EIT) were used to assess the participants’ gains in the knowledge of the target structures. In addition, language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) was measured and modelled as a predictor of gain scores. Results showed a significant effect of processing condition on GJT performance with the High DoP Implicit group outperforming the High DoP Explicit group on total scores and comparatives. In contrast, ANCOVA analyses indicated no significant group differences on EIT outcomes once pretest performance was controlled, with pretest scores strongly predicting posttest performance. In oral production, processing effects were structure-specific: the Low DoP group showed greater accuracy gains for comparatives, while both High DoP groups revealed increased frequency of use of third conditionals. However, across all four measures, multiple regression analyses indicated that LLAMA B, D, and F did not significantly predict gain scores. Overall, the findings support a processing-by-structure pattern: deeper processing benefits were most evident for the more salient structure (comparatives) on an explicit, written measure, whereas complex, low-salience forms (third conditionals) showed limited accuracy change but increased frequency of use under deeper processing.

title: A UAV-Based Framework for Community-Scale Residential Building Energy Modelling in China
authors: Mengfan Jin
abstract: With increasing emphasis on energy efficiency and carbon emission reduction in the building sector, rapid and scalable energy modelling of existing buildings is critical for retrofit projects and policy development. Conventional surveys, data collection and energy modelling processes remain labour-intensive and impractical for large-scale applications, and energy modelling often dominates project time and cost. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with high-resolution and infrared cameras now offer fast and safe exterior surveys, showing great potential in building energy assessments. Yet, a systematic framework for UAV integration, from image capture through processing to inputs for building energy simulation, has not been established. This research addresses these challenges by developing a structured framework for community-scale building energy modelling, which integrates UAV photogrammetry to accelerate data acquisition, reduce labour, and shorten energy modelling time for retrofit projects. The framework is designed to minimise prior data requirements while maximising automation and retaining sufficient accuracy and reliability. It also addressed systemic issues, such as the lack of data necessary to fully exploit the potential of available technologies in the context of this study. To achieve this research objective, a mixed-methodology approach, combining desk studies and fieldwork, was adopted. First, a comprehensive review of UAV-based building energy studies mapped the current applications and available tools, proposing a preliminary framework. Fieldwork then encompassed a pilot study and a detailed case study. In the pilot test, a single building was surveyed to identify an optimal toolchain for flight planning, image capture, photogrammetric reconstruction, model generation, and selection of a simulation platform. The resulting refined framework was applied to a case study of a 39-building community, and it was demonstrated that further automation was necessary. The potential for automation was then further explored. Geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and deep learning techniques were compared, and the combination that best balanced accuracy and processing time was selected for 3D model generation and window-to-wall ratio (WWR) extraction. In parallel, an archetype library of residential buildings in the Hot Summer Cold Winter (HSCW) zone in China was compiled to facilitate the assignment of thermal parameters. Finally, a reusable community-scale building energy modelling (CBEM) workflow was assembled in Grasshopper using Ladybug Tools components to process the aforementioned inputs. In conclusion, this study integrates UAV photogrammetry, GIS-based geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and graphical programming to develop an UAV-CBEM framework. The outcomes establish a foundation for scalable UAV-based building energy assessments, enhancing applicability in data-limited and large-scale settings worldwide.

title: Spectral Materialism: Encounters with land-time-scapes
authors: Nightingale, Sam
abstract: This transdisciplinary, practice-based PhD introduces spectral materialism through art-based research encounters with ecologically and historically stratified land-time-scapes shaped by hypersalinity and colonial terraforming. Centred in the semi-arid Mallee (southeastern Australia) and read through echoes with California’s Imperial Valley, the project examines how spectral time—the co-presence and haunting of other temporalities—manifests in the material conditions of salt, soil, water, plants, and infrastructures. It asks how learning from geological, First Nations, colonial, and ecological pasts can orient responsibilities in unsettled futures. Treating the present as a crisis of time as much as a crisis of matter, the thesis critiques linear-progressive temporalities bound to Western modernity and extractive regimes. In response, spectral materialism is developed as both a conceptual framework and a critical creative methodology. Through alchemical media experiments with salt crystals, hypersaline soils, and halophytes, photography is reconfigured as a site-responsive, process-oriented practice. Salt is engaged as a material agent and ‘time-crystal’ whose phase shifts—dissolution, saturation, precipitation, crystallisation, evaporation—form a meta-chemistry that refracts deep-marine pasts, settler-colonial irrigation infrastructures, and contemporary dust into processual renderings of time. Methodologically, the project advances attunement as a mode of sensing and responsiveness to forces that are not always immediately perceptible yet are materially active. Field notes appear as para-writing, interrupting linear narration so that heterogeneous times co-present themselves within the text. The thesis is guided by First Nations temporalities—time as relational and in place—while remaining accountable to ethical limits and protocols. The contribution is twofold: a theoretical articulation of spectral materialism as a way to think time otherwise, and a set of site-responsive methods for engaging elemental media in saline environments. Together, they generate materially grounded accounts of spectral presences and open alternative pathways for knowing, sensing, and relating within land-time-scapes marked by enduring colonial and ecological afterlives amid planetary change.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO ACCELERATE DERMATOLOGICAL DISCOVERY
authors: Jasson Makkar
abstract: The skin is the largest and outermost organ that surrounds the human body and provides a physical barrier that protects the more delicate internal tissues from the harsh surrounding environment. Over the course of evolution, specialized structures have also arisen in the skin, including sweat and sebaceous glands, nails and claws, and hair follicles. The hair follicle is a multi-lineage mini-organ that is a critical component in defining mammalian species. The gain of function derived from hair and fur benefited these species for millennia due to its insulative and protective properties, mechanosensing function, and ability to serve as camouflage. Current approaches to assess these fibers are generally non-quantitative or are low throughput due to technical limitations of ‘splitting hairs’. We developed a novel deep learning-based computer vision approach for the high throughput quantification of individual hair fibers at a high resolution. Our innovative computer vision tool can distinguish and extract overlapping fibers for quantification of multivariate features including length, width, and color to generate single-hair phenomes (shPhenome) of diverse conditions across the lifespan of mice. Using our tool, we explored the effects of hormone signaling, genetic modifications, and aging on hair follicle output. These analyses revealed novel hair phenotypes as a result of endocrinological, developmental, and aging-related alterations in the fur coats of mice. This tool was then adapted to capture more nuanced hair phenotypes, such as curvature, in a variety of mouse models harboring genetic perturbations. Commercialization of the deep hair phenomics technology presented a unique opportunity to pursue research translation, transforming fundamental biological research into marketable products. Much like the traditional academic route, the path to commercialization requires consistent and continuous iteration, testing of hypotheses, and allowing data to influence and lead subsequent actions. However, as opposed to the pursuit of knowledge, translating research into market-ready solutions requires a focus on consumer needs and the identification of market opportunities. Additionally, the shift in incentive structure requires commercial ventures to prioritize intellectual property protection, alter capital and resource allocation, and seek alternative fundraising sources. The entrepreneurial foundation built through this process culminated in the filing of a provisional patent and establishment of a startup company, kerat Inc. This journey illuminated the multifaceted challenges inherent in closing the gap between academic innovation and commercially viable goods, requiring simultaneous advancement of technical capabilities, adaptation to market dynamics, and fabrication of business infrastructure. Overall, the culmination of work presented in this dissertation sheds light on the importance of quantitatively assessing hair fiber properties to capture the biological phenomena that underlie this fundamental feature of mammalian skin. These findings also highlight the capabilities of this methodology for identifying perturbations in normal growth, potentially indicative of disease or dysfunction. Lastly, this showcased the potential of this technology’s commercial use cases in both the cosmetics and diagnostics industries.
